title: Indentation & Comments Practice
instructions: In the coding window, you'll see a comment and an `if` statement. Your job is to indent the `print()` statement using exactly 4 spaces so the program runs. Notice how Python ignores the note at the top!
steps: Identify the comment on line 1 (starting with #)
Look at the if statement on line 2
Add exactly 4 spaces before the print statement on line 3
Run the code to see your message!
Bonus: Try changing the text inside the print quotes!
hints: Python ignores lines starting with #, so leave line 1 as it is.
Use exactly 4 spaces for each level of indentation.
The print statement must be 'inside' the if block by being pushed to the right.
Ensure you don't delete the quotes around your text!

tests.name: Check for comment usage
Check exact indentation (4 spaces)
tests.code:
lines = code.split('\n')
print_line = next((l for l in lines if l.lstrip().startswith('print')), None)
if print_line is None:
    raise AssertionError('Could not find a print() statement in your code.')
leading = len(print_line) - len(print_line.lstrip(' '))
if leading != 4:
    raise AssertionError(f'The print statement must start with exactly 4 spaces. Found {leading}.')
print('TEST_PASSED: Correct indentation')

tests.name: Check that the greeting was printed
tests.expected: The print statement runs and produces its message
